title: A Lie-algebraic approach to non-Markovian quantum dynamics
authors: Haijin Ding, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Zhiwen Zhang
abstract: In this paper, we study the non-Markovian quantum dynamics in quantum computations from the perspective of a Lie algebraic approach based on numerical analysis. By vectorizing the density matrix of quantum states, the non-Markovian evolutions can be represented with high-dimensional linear time-varying equations, where the time-varying parameters arise from the non-Markovian interactions between the quantum system and environment. We study the Magnus expansion of such linear time-varying quantum dynamics and clarify how the truncation errors for the first- and second-order Magnus expansions are influenced by the non-Markovian properties. Besides, when the quantum states are measured for filtering, the dynamics can be modeled as time-varying stochastic differential equations due to the existence of measurement noise. The Magnus expansions based on quantum stochastic filtering are different when the quantum measurement noises are modeled in an {Itô} or Stratonovich approach, rendering different truncation errors. Based on this, numerical simulations further demonstrate the efficiency of Magnus expansions in simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics without or with stochasticity, and how the truncation errors are influenced by the Lie algebras in the Liouville space.
summary: This paper develops a Lie algebraic framework to analyze and simulate non-Markovian quantum dynamics. By mapping the density matrix evolution into a high-dimensional linear time-varying system, it applies the Magnus expansion technique. The key contribution is providing detailed error analysis showing how truncation errors depend on non-Markovian effects and the choice of stochastic calculus (Itô vs. Stratonovich) during measurement.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, particularly when measurement noise is involved.
main_result: It demonstrates that the Magnus expansion can efficiently simulate these complex dynamics, and it rigorously quantifies how truncation errors depend on the underlying Lie algebraic structure and whether the stochastic process is modeled using Itô or Stratonovich calculus.
method: The core methodology involves vectorizing the density matrix to transform the evolution into a high-dimensional linear time-varying equation in Liouville space, which is then solved using the Magnus expansion technique derived from Lie algebra theory.
model_or_system: The model describes an open quantum system interacting with an environment. The dynamics are governed by equations that transition from standard Lindblad forms to complex stochastic differential equations (SDEs) when measurement/filtering is included.
key_observables: Truncation errors of the first- and second-order Magnus expansions, and the comparison between Itô and Stratonovich noise models in quantum filtering.
important_parameters: The step size ($h$) for numerical integration, and the time scale relative to non-Markovian interaction timescales.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating higher-order terms of the Magnus expansion using Taylor series expansions around a midpoint, and assumes bounded time-varying amplitudes in the Liouville equation representation.
figures_summary: Numerical simulations compare ideal evolution trajectories against results from first-order Runge-Kutta (RK) methods and second-order Magnus expansions, showing good agreement only for very short simulation times.
paper_structure: The paper builds theoretically by representing non-Markovian dynamics as linear time-varying equations in the Liouville space using a Lie algebraic basis. It then applies and analyzes the convergence properties of the Magnus expansion for both deterministic and stochastic (Itô/Stratonovich) regimes, concluding with numerical validation.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced mathematical tools (Lie algebra, Magnus expansion) to tackle the notoriously difficult problem of non-Markovian dynamics in quantum computing contexts, offering rigorous error analysis that is crucial for developing reliable quantum simulators.
